parisDakar.title: Send a parcel from Paris to Dakar
parisDakar.lead: Paris–Dakar is Yadony's most active corridor: the Senegalese community of the Paris region sends parcels to Dakar every week, and travellers fly the route in both directions all year round.
parisDakar.how: Publish your parcel in the app with its weight, description and photo. Verified travellers flying from Paris to Dakar see your request and offer their price per kilo. You choose, hand the parcel over in person in the Paris region, and your relative collects it in Dakar from the traveller.
parisDakar.price: The price per kilo is set freely by each traveller according to their flight and baggage allowance. You compare listings before choosing. A service commission, always shown before payment, is deducted from the transaction.
parisDakar.delay: A direct Paris–Dakar flight takes about 5.5 hours. Your parcel arrives on the day of the traveller's flight: from handover, you know the exact date, and the pick-up in Dakar is arranged in the days after landing.
parisDakar.safety: Traveller identity verified with Didit, card payment held until delivery is confirmed, handover validated with a 6-digit code, every step time-stamped and geolocated. Your loved one follows everything from a simple web page, no account needed.

faq.question: How much does sending a parcel Paris–Dakar cost?
faq.answer: The traveller sets their price per kilo; you compare listings before choosing. For a 5 kg parcel with a traveller at 8 euros per kilo, the traveller receives 40 euros and you pay 40 euros plus the service fee, shown before payment.

faq.question: How long does a parcel take to reach Dakar?
faq.answer: The traveller's flight time (about 5.5 hours direct), plus the handover appointment in Dakar. You see the departure date before booking, so you know from the start when your parcel arrives.

faq.question: How does my relative collect the parcel in Dakar?
faq.answer: The traveller and the recipient agree on a meeting. At handover, the recipient gives the 6-digit code you passed on to them and the traveller takes a photo: delivery is confirmed and the traveller's payment is released.

faq.answer: Anything legal and declared: clothes, non-regulated medicines, non-official documents, everyday products. Prohibited items include drugs, weapons, counterfeits, live animals and identity documents. The traveller sees your full declaration before accepting.

faq.question: How is the payment protected?
faq.answer: By card, you are charged when the traveller accepts, but the money stays held on the platform: the traveller is only paid after delivery is confirmed, with the 6-digit code you pass on to the recipient. If the shipment is cancelled before handover, you get a full refund.

parisBamako.title: Send a parcel from Paris to Bamako
parisBamako.lead: From Montreuil to Seine-Saint-Denis, the Malian diaspora of the Paris region has long entrusted parcels to whoever is flying home. Yadony puts a proper framework around that habit: to send a parcel from Paris to Bamako, you pick a traveller whose identity has been verified and follow your shipment right through to handover.
parisBamako.how: There are two ways to go about it. Browse the Paris–Bamako trips posted by travellers and book space in their suitcase, or post your own shipping request (weight, contents, photos) and let travellers send you offers. You then arrange a meeting in the Paris region, near Charles de Gaulle or Orly for instance, and the traveller scans the parcel's QR code the moment you hand it over.
parisBamako.price: Each traveller picks their own pricing: a rate per kilo, a per-item price list (a box of clothes, a phone, tins of baby formula) or an openness to price offers. So you can discuss the amount before committing. Yadony's service fee is always shown before you pay.
parisBamako.delay: If the traveller has a direct flight, allow about 5.5 hours to Bamako-Sénou airport; with a stopover, the journey often takes between 8 and 14 hours depending on the connection. You see the departure date before booking, and the parcel arrives with the traveller, not weeks later at the bottom of a shipping container.
parisBamako.safety: The traveller has verified their identity (ID document and selfie, with Didit or Stripe Identity) before posting their trip. Whether you pay by card, mobile money or from your Yadony wallet, the money is held until delivery. Your family in Bamako follows every stage (handed over, in flight, arrived, delivered) on a web page, without creating an account.

faq.question: Can I pay for a Bamako shipment with mobile money?
faq.answer: Yes. As well as card and your Yadony wallet, you can pay with mobile money (Orange Money, Moov, Wave or MTN, depending on the operators available), which is handy if you hold an account in CFA francs. Just as with a card, the amount is held until delivery is confirmed.

faq.question: What if I would rather pay the traveller in cash?
faq.answer: You can if the traveller agrees, but the money then bypasses escrow: Yadony can neither hold it until delivery nor refund you if something goes wrong. For a valuable parcel, paying in the app remains the safest option.

faq.question: How does the handover work in Bamako?
faq.answer: The traveller and your recipient agree on a time and place after landing. Your relative gives the 6-digit collection code you passed on to them, the traveller takes a geotagged photo, and delivery is confirmed: only then is the traveller paid.

lyonDakar.delay: Between Lyon and Dakar, the journey often involves a stopover, in Paris or elsewhere: expect 8 to 12 hours in many cases, depending on the connection. At handover, they scan the parcel's QR code and take a geotagged photo; you then watch it move from handed over to in flight, arrived and delivered. Payment by card, Wave, Orange Money or wallet stays held until your recipient gives their 6-digit code.
